exposure: Combined intervention of Manchester Pain Management Model (MPMM) and empowerment education
outcome: First independent time out of bed activity
cohort: The study included 120 women who underwent cesarean section in a hospital between June 2021 and June 2023.
finding: The combined intervention of the Manchester pain management model and empowerment education significantly improved postoperative pain control, accelerated physiological recovery, and increased overall satisfaction with nursing care compared to standard nursing measures.
mod_finding: The combined intervention significantly improved pain scores, accelerated physiological recovery (e.g., first time out of bed, first exhaust gas), reduced length of hospital stay, and increased breastfeeding success and nursing satisfaction after cesarean section.
followup_time: Up to 24 hours post-surgery and through hospital stay (length of hospital stay was an outcome)
